artworks.title: Plate Number 725. Lion walking and turning around
artworks.description: This is a series of twelve black-and-white photographs depicting a lion in motion. The images show the lion walking along a plain backdrop, capturing different positions of its movement. The background is minimal to emphasize the dynamism and power of the lion's steps.

artworks.title: Plate Number 726. Lion and lioness walking
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequential motion study featuring lions. The series consists of twelve black-and-white frames, each capturing two lions walking side by side in a lateral sequence. The frames are arranged in four rows, each row depicting a gradual change in the position of the lions as they move across the view from left to right. The background is a simple, likely wooden surface, providing a plain backdrop that emphasizes the movement of the lions. The texture of the ground they walk on is rough and natural. The lions' progression in slight variations in stance and stride gives a sense of rhythm and methodology common in early motion photography studies aimed at understanding animal movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 727. Lioness walking and lion lying down
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of twelve black and white images showing a lioness interacting with a lion. The images display the lioness approaching and engaging with the lion, who is lying down facing her. The background consists of a plain wall and a dirt or gravel surface. The images suggest a gentle interaction and potential communication between the two animals as the lioness moves closer to the lion. Each frame shows a slight change in movement, giving a sense of progression through the sequence.

artworks.title: Plate Number 728. Lioness walking

Each frame showcases subtle changes in the lioness's posture as she walks, focusing on the movement of her legs and tail. The monochrome images provide a scientific and artistic evaluation of animal locomotion.

The photographs appear to be part of a study capturing the details of the tiger's movement.

Each frame provides a different perspective of the tiger's gait.

artworks.title: Plate Number 731. Jaguar. A: Walking. B: Turning around

artworks.title: Plate Number 732. Elephant walking

artworks.title: Plate Number 733. Elephant walking

The elephant moves from one side of the frame to the other, presented in a scientific or documentary style.

The series demonstrates a study of motion, highlighting the nuances in the camel's gait. The images offer a detailed analysis of the camel's locomotion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 741. Bactrian camel. A: Walking. B: Racking

The photographs are likely part of a motion study series, capturing detailed dynamic movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 744. Raccoon walking, changing to a gallop

The frames are numbered to track the sequence of gait. The raccoon, with its banded tail and masked face, is the central focus of this analysis of motion.

The grid serves as a reference for observing the animal's actions with accuracy. The sequence documents the nuances of the raccoon's gait in a scientific manner.

The frames showcase the natural movement of the capybara's legs and body as it walks on a flat surface, resembling early motion studies in photography.

artworks.title: Plate Number 748. Baboon walking on all fours
